title.en: Breakable joint measurement and threshold contract

summary: Release a constraint from a declared solver measurement with compatible units and an explicit unsupported-backend fallback.
objective: A joint breaks once for a traceable threshold crossing, while render motion cannot masquerade as reaction-force measurement.
applies_when: A machine connector, destructible prop or educational joint releases in response to simulated loading.
intent_signals: break a joint when force exceeds a limit
example_prompts: Make a hanging prop detach when its measured joint load exceeds the declared limit.
Explain why copying the Blender breakable threshold into a browser force slider is unsafe.
negative_signals: infer joint force from mesh speed
sum force and torque without units
not_for: Predicting real material failure, crack propagation or certified structural safety.
An authored break animation whose trigger is intentionally scripted rather than load-driven.

principles: Choose the backend and exact supported measurement before offering a load-triggered break control. A source-level possibility is not a callable browser API.

Specify quantity, units, coordinate frame, selected axes, sign or magnitude rule, sampling interval and threshold comparison. Keep linear and angular quantities separate; never take a mixed-unit spatial-vector norm as a physical load.
A contact event, displacement error or body velocity is not automatically a joint reaction. Label an intentionally chosen proxy as an approximation with its own rule.
Constraint release is a simulation state transition. Three.js displays the resulting body poses; particles, sound and cracks may decorate the event without causing or measuring it.
implementation: In Blender author separate pieces, stable connector/body IDs, joint frames, collision shapes and reset poses. Treat exported geometry and any custom connector description separately; reconstruct constraints explicitly in the chosen runtime.

Inspect the installed solver binding for a supported post-step joint measurement and its interval semantics. The reviewed Rapier JavaScript ImpulseJoint page supplies no documented reaction getter; do not invent joint.impulse() or substitute a contact-force event. Use a verified adapter/backend, a declared baked playback, or clearly labeled scripted release when measurement is unavailable.

For supported measurements, sample at the documented simulation boundary. If a reported linear impulse covers delta_t, convert to average force only using that same nonzero interval; do not use render-frame time, blindly sum warm-start accumulators, or claim this average is a peak.

Compare the declared component or like-unit magnitude to its matching threshold. State any persistence or filtering policy and the delay it introduces; a per-step impulse threshold and an average-force threshold describe different rules.

Queue joint removal once at a backend-safe boundary, preserve the dynamic bodies current poses and velocities, and update connector state and any collision-filter policy deliberately. Do not inject an extra explosion impulse unless it is a separately declared effect.

Reset recreates original bodies/constraints or restores a supported complete baseline, clears pending break events and measurement history, restores filters, and resets render interpolation so a broken pose does not leak into the next run.
observable_checks: A later authorized check records backend/version, measured quantity, source API, units, interval and threshold alongside one intact-to-broken event; unavailable readout produces an explicit unsupported state.
Use a scoped below/above-threshold fixture and reset: release occurs once and reset restores the intended constraint and collision configuration. These are proposed checks, not results.

Change render cadence while holding the simulation step and inputs fixed; the trigger consumes simulation samples only. Any later step-size comparison must keep force-versus-impulse semantics explicit rather than demand universal numerical invariance.
Inspect release continuity and label any visual-only burst; unsupported joint measurement is never represented by a working measured-force slider.

creative_affordances: Choose whimsical detachable lanterns, mechanical latches or educational load indicators without prescribing a realistic art style.
Use a scripted break for storytelling when it is honestly presented as authored behavior.
known_limits: An impulse/force threshold is a simplified release rule, not validated fracture mechanics.
The JavaScript API-page observation does not rule out supported future versions or explicitly verified custom bindings.
No Blender export, solver, renderer, browser or threshold fixture was executed.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5 exposes Breakable for rigid-body constraints except Motor, and describes Threshold as the impulse strength required to break the constraint.
claims.scope: Blender authoring setting, not a force value or an automatically transported runtime constraint.

source_refs.locator: Common Options / Settings: Breakable and Threshold

claims.statement: The Rapier JavaScript ImpulseJoint API page read on 2026-09-08 lists anchors, bodies, frames, contact settings, validity and type methods; it does not document a public joint-reaction force or impulse getter.
claims.scope: Bounded observation of this JavaScript API page; no claim that every Rapier version, Rust API, raw binding or third-party adapter lacks such access.

source_refs.locator: Complete public methods index and method descriptions

claims.statement: For a force integrated over a nonzero time interval, linear impulse J equals the average force over that same interval multiplied by its duration, so F_avg = J / delta_t.
claims.scope: Vector relation for the same measured interval; an average is not an instantaneous peak force or a material fracture law.
